Hi, thanks for the contribution. 

As I mentioned in the original proposal, I am very wary about adding additional data stored in the TileMapLayer. It can lead to huge increases in memory usage if users do not pay attention to the data they store there. Also, I do not want to bloat the API more than it already is. 

While I understand why users want this, I already mentioned in other proposals that TileMapLayer is not a "scene placer". It needs to be kept optimized for the most part, which this PR goes against.

To solve the original problem, I suggested to implement a built-in tool to place scenes into a grid, as children of a given node in the scene tree. Such a tool could "borrow" the grid settings of a given TileMapLayer if needed, so that you don't have to reconfigure it every time. This would probably solve most of the original issue, without bloating the TileMapLayer API, and while making all scene perfectly editable from withing the scene tree.

> It can lead to huge increases in memory usage if users do not pay attention to the data they store there

u mean in run time or storage?

> u mean in run time or storage?

Yeah sorry, I meant mainly storage. But that increases loading time too.

To make it clear, one of the advantages of using reference to scenes is that each `.tscn` is only loaded once, independently on how many instances you place. If we started storing data in TileMapLayer's data, then each cell would need to update the instantiated scene which can get pretty heavy with several thousands of tiles.

With the current implementation, all cells don't store data; only the changed value is stored
So no need for all tiles to be updated

> With the current implementation, all cells don't store data; only the changed value is stored

Yeah. Still if you change the value, then paint 1000 tiles with this changed value, you end up with this same value copied a thousand time in the TileMapLayer data, which is not acceptable.

> > With the current implementation, all cells don't store data; only the changed value is stored
> 
> Yeah. Still if you change the value, then paint 1000 tiles with this changed value, you end up with this same value copied a thousand time in the TileMapLayer data, which is not acceptable.

Can we calculate how much it can cost?

> 1000 tiles

This value is out of reality, nobody places 1000 tiles of scene in a single level.
The most common use case of TileMap is using texture as tile, and tile scenes are just for a couple of things like enemies, loot boxes, etc...

> Can we calculate how much it can cost?

No, and that's a the main problem. It depends on what users expose in their scenes, and how they use it.
TileMapLayer has a very short and limited amount of data per cell (I think around 128bits or something). Simply storing a string could multiply the storage by significant factors if you don't pay attention.

That's why I suggested the other, scene painting solution, as it makes this cost a lot more obvious (everything ends up in the scene-tree, is visible in the text `.tscn`, and users are already used to it.

> This value is out of reality, nobody places 1000 tiles of scene in a single level.
The most common use case of TileMap is using texture as tile, and tile scenes are just for a couple of things like enemies, loot boxes, etc...

Many different kind of games use tilemap. Some use scenes to paint animated trees, grass, whatever... So that's not unrealistic in a huge world. In any case, without making the cost of using such properties obvious to users, it cannot be merged. But anyway, the scene-painting solution is simply better. It should be not a lot of code, and should involve editor-changes only. (see my comment there for an even simpler solution: https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/7249#issuecomment-1630358375 )

If you meant in the TileMapLayer node, I think it's not really necessary, and it would cause issues if you end up with discrepancies between what's stored in the TileMapLayer vs scene tree.

Currently, using scene collections as TilemapLayers aren't very flexible or useful compared to dragging nodes directly into the scene, especially since positional offsets can't even be set manually. This looks extremely useful by comparison, allowing single scenes to be made and modified directly in the TilemapLayer, eradicating the need for making endless amounts of instanced scenes and bloating the scene collections with duplicates for different types of scenes:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9aa46ccd-5d8b-4595-b941-ff548f8bb34c

As appears in the video, I would say that would be a huge improvement over manual placing of scenes and allow the scene collection TilemapLayers to be considered as a timesaver. Currently, they're neither more organizational nor more efficient if multiple types of the same scene are needed.

> Currently, using scene collections as TilemapLayers aren't very flexible or useful compared to dragging nodes directly into the scene, especially since positional offsets can't even be set manually. This looks extremely useful by comparison, allowing single scenes to be made and modified directly in the TilemapLayer, eradicating the need for making endless amounts of instanced scenes and bloating the scene collections with duplicates for different types of scenes:

I don't deny the usefulness of it. My main problem with it is that it could store a ton of data in the user's back (which is a significant performance problem) and it would make the TileMapLayer API even more complex (it's already a super complex and bloated API). 

Having scene in the scene tree makes a lot more sense here anyway, as it gives you all the current existing tools to edit them, and solve the problem of knowing the performance impact. Having a  "scene placer" tool to do that should easily solve the mentioned usability problem.

> As appears in the video, I would say that would be a huge improvement over manual placing of scenes and allow the scene collection TilemapLayers to be considered as a timesaver. Currently, they're neither more organizational nor more efficient if multiple types of the same scene are needed.

Yeah I agree, sadly we cannot add such band-aid solution as this would be a nightmare to keep compatibility. I hope someone can tackle the task of implementing such a scene painting tool instead though.

I think it does not even require a node. I think it should be a tool in the top toolbar of the 2D editor. Something like a "paint" mode. When you select it, you get additional configuration in the top toolbar. Likely:
1) a packed scene selector (to select what is going to be painted)
1) a node selector (similar to what you have in the inspector), to select the parent where nodes are going to be added.
3) a configuration menu to setup a grid, with a way to select a TileMapLayer as source for the config.
